REGIONAL REGULATION OF JOMBANG REGENCY

NUMBER 14. YEAR 2008

REGARDING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

The objective of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide is to provide protection and services for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of women and children.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Article 5

Article 6

What is meant by obtaining protection is obtaining protection from the family, Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Advocates, Social Institutions or other parties, either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court, husband, wife and children.

What is meant by obtaining information is knowing about the existence of complaint centers, P2T-P2A and or other competent companion institutions regarding matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

What is meant by integrated services is services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial, legal and socio-political. What is meant by continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of good name and the victim has the right to obtain socio-economic empowerment.

What is meant by the victim having the right to report is that the victim can report acts of violence to the P2T-P2A Secretariat of Jombang Regency or Jombang Police (UPPA), or Women's Crisis Center (WCC) Jombang. What is meant by obtaining psychological and legal assistance is obtaining psychological and legal assistance at every level of examination and during the judicial process.

Sufficiently clear

T

Article 3

The best interests of the victim is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men and all actions that deprive children of their rights and freedoms.

This excerpt sits under: CHAPTER II

Article 2

Number 1

Respect for the rights of victims is intended for the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Number 2 i

Gender justice is a process to become fair to men and women;

Number 3

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

Article 5

Every victim has the right to report and obtain assistance both psychologically and legally and obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 7

The Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2T-P2A).

Article 8

of services for victims organized by P2T-P2A include:

a. Medical services, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics; b. Medicolegal services constitute a form of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the legal field; which
c. Psychosocial services constitute services provided by assistants to help restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses that protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims as well as provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems or undergoing legal processes;
d. Legal assistance services to victims during the legal process;
e. Socio-political services in the form of policy advocacy that is preventive and curative in nature for victims.
(2) The service mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized according to the Standard Operational Procedure (SOP) which will be further regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 4

Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, ongoing handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or Government and non-Government institutions.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

CHAPTER VI ASSISTANCE

Article 10

Assistance is carried out by a person or institution that has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims who are members of the P2T-P2A Management Team.

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

c. Psychosocial services constitute services provided by assistants to help restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses that protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims as well as provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems or undergoing legal processes;
d. Legal assistance services to victims during the legal process;
e. Socio-political services in the form of policy advocacy that is preventive and curative in nature for victims.
(2) The service mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized according to the Standard Operational Procedure (SOP) which will be further regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 3

The best interests of the victim is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3

Number 3

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

Article 7

The Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2T-P2A).

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF JOMBANG REGENCY

NUMBER 14. YEAR 2008

REGARDING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

The objective of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide is to provide protection and services for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of women and children.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 2

Number 1

Respect for the rights of victims is intended for the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Number 2 i

Gender justice is a process to become fair to men and women;

Number 3

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

Article 4

Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, ongoing handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or Government and non-Government institutions.

Article 5

Every victim has the right to report and obtain assistance both psychologically and legally and obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 3

The best interests of the victim is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men and all actions that deprive children of their rights and freedoms.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.
